title: Uncovering the Mechanistic Landscape of Regulatory DNA with Deep Learning.
authors: Seitz, Evan E; McCandlish, David M; Kinney, Justin B; Koo, Peter K
journal: bioRxiv : the preprint server for biology
one_liner_zh: 该文用深度学习与可解释AI框架SEAM解析调控DNA中转录因子结合位点及突变对结合的影响，核心聚焦TF-DNA互作机制建模，高度匹配本课题。
abstract: The regulatory genome encodes the logic that governs gene expression, enabling cells to respond to developmental, environmental, and evolutionary cues. This logic arises from complex cis-regulatory mechanisms that integrate transcription factor motifs, their syntactical arrangement, and surrounding sequence context, features that remain challenging to decode. Here, we present SEAM (Systematic Explanation of Attribution-based Mechanisms), a computational framework that combines deep learning with explainable AI to map the mechanistic impact of genetic mutations. Applied to human and Drosophila regulatory loci, SEAM uncovers functional binding sites at sequences of interest and identifies which mutations preserve, disrupt, or create novel binding sites. SEAM also reveals that two qualitatively distinct classes of regulatory signal are operative at many loci: signals that are robust to mutation and signals that are readily reprogrammable. These results clarify the inherent ability of regulatory DNA to evolve. They also position SEAM as a versatile framework for interpreting non-coding variants and for informing the mechanism-aware design of synthetic sequences.
abstract_zh: 调控基因组编码了支配基因表达的逻辑，使细胞能够响应发育、环境和进化信号。这一逻辑源于复杂的顺式调控机制，这些机制整合了转录因子基序、其句法排列及周围序列背景，而这些特征至今仍难以解码。在此，我们提出SEAM（基于归因机制的系统性解释），这是一个结合深度学习与可解释人工智能的计算框架，用于绘制基因突变的机制性影响。应用于人类和果蝇的调控位点，SEAM在目标序列中揭示功能性结合位点，并识别哪些突变保留、破坏或创造新的结合位点。SEAM还揭示，在许多位点上存在两类性质不同的调控信号：一类对突变具有稳健性，另一类则易于重编程。这些结果阐明了调控DNA固有的进化能力，同时将SEAM定位为一个多功能框架，用于解读非编码变异并指导基于机制的合成序列设计。
